newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian magistrates question ex-Olivetti man.
newsitem.headline: Italian magistrates question ex-Olivetti man.

text.p: Italian magistrates probing information and technology company Olivetti said on Saturday they had questioned the troubled firm's former director general, Renzo Francesconi.

Magistrates in the town of Ivrea, where Olivetti is based, said they had questioned Francesconi "as a person informed of the facts" for more than nine hours in a marathon session that ended early on Saturday.
"The length of the session was due to the complexity of the questions we tackled," deputy prosecutor Alberto Braghin told reporters.

Francesconi resigned from the loss-making group nearly two weeks ago shortly after the company announced the resignation of chairman Carlo De Benedetti and said it had made a 440.2 billion lire ($288 million) loss for the first half of 1996.

Francesconi made comments at the time of stepping down which cast doubts on the accuracy of the group's accounts and has since been questioned by stock market watchdog Consob in a separate probe into the state of Olivetti's finances.

Braghin said prosecutors had yet to place anyone under formal investigation in the Ivrea probe, which was opened after small investors' group Assorisparmio lodged a formal complaint with Ivrea magistrates concerning Olivetti.
The group's share price has fallen steadily on the stock market in the last year but plummetted around 28 percent to record lows at the start of this week as Consob's investigation deepened.
